correctness.rationale: The fixed-point inclusion-exclusion mass and its independent binomial mixture give \(R_k=(1-\theta)^n Q_k(\theta/(1-\theta))\). Exact polynomial identities \(Q_1^2-Q_0Q_2=nr^2\) and \(Q_0Q_3-Q_1^2=nr+n(2n-3)r^2+n(n-1)(n-2)r^3\), together with \(Q_2>Q_1\) and monotonicity of \(Q_k\), strictly sort all attainable two-game outcomes at the total-two likelihood threshold, including the \(n=4\) support gap. Neyman-Pearson proves the identical test is optimal for every 0<theta<1. Direct randomization arithmetic yields the triangular difference AB/(A+B) n theta^2(1-theta)^(2n-2) h(alpha); derangement convergence proves the sparse-intensity coefficient. All 32 rational exact diagnostics and selected sparse settings passed from the embedded standalone verifier; they are supplementary, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: In repeated matching tests, the observed vector of match counts and their total are two natural competing data reductions. The theorem resolves the first genuinely ambiguous total (two matches) for every possible sample size n>=4 and every positive skill strength, giving one UMP ordering independent of the alternative, an exact continuum of optimal size/power losses, and a sharp sparse-skill correction. This is a motivated conditional-testing boundary, not an arbitrary isolated parameter value. It measures exactly what information total aggregation discards and when that loss matters; the significance band is stated explicitly, with no claim for conventional 5% tests.
